description.p: Zeke is a native TIDAL player for Linux, built for hi-res lossless playback (up to 24-bit/192 kHz FLAC). It can play through ALSA in exclusive mode, bit-perfect when the output device takes the track’s rate and with one high-quality resample when it doesn’t, and it is gapless across tracks in every mode.

ul.li: Home feed, search, favorites, and album, playlist, artist and mix pages
A queue that is saved and comes back where you left it
Shuffle, repeat, ReplayGain and a quality badge for the stream
Media keys and desktop integration through MPRIS

description.p: Favorites → Playlists now follows your TIDAL library: Loved Tracks first, then your folders, then your playlists, with who made each one and how many tracks it has. Open a folder to see what is in it, and sort by last updated, date added or name. Folders are read only for now.
Upcoming tracks can be removed from the queue: each one has a remove button in the queue list. The track playing and the ones already played stay.
Resuming after a long pause no longer fails with a 403 error: the track is loaded again with fresh stream URLs and picks up where it was paused.
Pausing with an exclusive output no longer freezes the player until a restart. Zeke now also keeps a log of its last few runs in ~/.local/state/zeke, for reporting problems.

Continuous playback. When the queue runs out with repeat off, Zeke keeps going with the radio of its last track, gaplessly, and says so when the radio takes over. It is on by default and can be turned off in Preferences › Playback.

TIDAL radio. Every track's menu goes to its radio, the artist page has a Radio button, and so does Now Playing for the track that is playing. The station opens as a page, labelled Track Radio or Artist Radio, to play or shuffle from there.
The player bar has shuffle and repeat, which were only in Now Playing. Repeat shows a loop in every mode, and the speaker icon of the output menu is the size of the icons around it.

Groundwork for plugins, with no change to how Zeke looks or plays. The saved TIDAL session now records when its tokens were issued, so Zeke can tell a token that is about to expire. Settings that a future plugin saves are kept by every settings change and token refresh.

An output menu in the player bar: play through the system default or on a sound device exclusively, with bit-perfect playback per device. Zeke takes the card from PipeWire when it plays and gives it back afterwards, and falls back to the system default when the device is busy.
The first version: TIDAL login, browsing, hi-res gapless playback, a saved queue, favorites and keyboard shortcuts.
